content.text:
No, it isn't safe by default, but the docs give you a fix.

- **Use `prefix(...)`.** `@import "tailwindcss" prefix(tw);` prefixes both classes and theme variables. The compiled output has `--tw-color-red-500` and `.tw\:text-red-500` (`styling-with-utility-classes.mdx`, "Using the prefix option"). Utilities such as `rounded-lg` still work.
- **Only output what's used.** Theme variables are generated only when used, unless you set `@theme static` (`theme.mdx`, "Generating all CSS variables"). Your CSS therefore only defines the variables your utilities actually use, such as the radius ones behind `rounded-lg`.
- **Drop the defaults.** `--*: initial;` in `@theme` clears all default variables so only yours remain (`theme.mdx`, "Sharing across projects" and the preceding custom-theme section).

The docs don't say how to ship a library to third-party sites, so I'm inferring that `prefix()` is the safe route for you. Your own custom `--color-*` names would still be unprefixed unless you define them under the prefix too.

No, it isn't safe by default, but the docs give you a fix.

- **Use `prefix(...)`.** `@import "tailwindcss" prefix(tw);` prefixes both classes and theme variables. The compiled output has `--tw-color-red-500` and `.tw\:text-red-500` (`styling-with-utility-classes.mdx`, "Using the prefix option"). Utilities such as `rounded-lg` still work.
- **Only output what's used.** Theme variables are generated only when used, unless you set `@theme static` (`theme.mdx`, "Generating all CSS variables"). Your CSS therefore only defines the variables your utilities actually use, such as the radius ones behind `rounded-lg`.
- **Drop the defaults.** `--*: initial;` in `@theme` clears all default variables so only yours remain (`theme.mdx`, "Sharing across projects" and the preceding custom-theme section).

The docs don't say how to ship a library to third-party sites, so I'm inferring that `prefix()` is the safe route for you. Your own custom `--color-*` names would still be unprefixed unless you define them under the prefix too.
